ShortDescription.Value: Apply custom surfaces to road pavement, sidewalks, bike lanes and bus lanes, with reusable presets and junction controls.

## AI development and maintenance disclaimer
This mod was made using AI. I am not a developer and have zero programming knowledge, so I may struggle to fix bugs, keep the mod working after game updates, or maintain it over time.
Source code, bug reports and maintenance enquiries can be found on the project's [GitHub](https://github.com/Andy123k1/RoadSurfaceFiller) page, which you can find through the [official Cities: Skylines Modding Discord](https://discord.gg/HTav7ARPs2).
If you are a developer willing to help maintain the mod or take over the project, please contact me through that Discord. I am happy to discuss handing over the GitHub repository so the project can continue to be supported.
# Road Surface Filler
Give your roads custom pavement, sidewalk, bike-lane and bus-lane finishes using the surfaces installed in your game.
## Features - Create reusable surface presets for different roads and lanes. - See surface thumbnail previews beside finishes in the surface pickers. - Choose whether editing a preset updates roads already using it or keeps their existing finishes. - Choose a preset while drawing roads, or use the road tool's Replace mode to restyle existing segments. - Apply general rules to existing roads with Apply city rules. - Activate the junction cycler and click junctions directly to cycle connected road and bus-lane finishes while keeping bike-lane surfaces visible. Right-click to exit the tool. - Fill adjacent paved bus-lane shoulders, or remove that shoulder fill from selected roads. - Convert generated surfaces into independent editable areas, with a tool to resume automatic updates later. - Restore selected roads or all roads to vanilla surfaces. - Manage rules in a movable, resizable panel with collapsible rule cards.
## Getting started Open the RSF button beside the Info button. Create a preset under Segment rules, then select it in the road tool's Surface rule picker. To apply general rules across existing roads, create them under General rules and choose Apply city rules.
Under Tools, choose Cycle junction surface, then left-click a junction or roundabout in the city. Each click advances its finish, and the tool stays active until you right-click or choose Exit junction tool.
## Manual surface editing Under Tools, choose Make generated surfaces editable, then click a completed road segment. Its surfaces become independent and the editor opens automatically. Drag boundary points or add points along edges to reshape them; each area keeps its existing finish. Use Edit another segment to convert additional roads and all approaches of a junction or roundabout. Finish editing exits the editor. Right-click cancels a drag; right-click while idle exits. Automatic updates stop on converted roads, and manual areas survive rebuilds, rule changes and road changes, including road removal. Restore all roads keeps these independent areas. Resume automatic surfaces reactivates saved road rules while keeping manual areas, so remove unwanted overlaps yourself. Keep this mod and the relevant surface assets enabled for these areas to render.
## Surface packs This mod uses available surface assets; it does not include the custom surface packs shown in screenshots. Install the packs containing the finishes you want to use. Only surfaces that support rendering over roads appear in the surface pickers. Those packs may have their own dependencies.
## Saved cities Segment finishes, junction choices and named styling profiles are saved with each city. Each profile contains its own General rules and Segment rules. Default starts with your shared rules from before the update. Create an empty profile or duplicate Default for a new city's style. Use the Profiles tab to copy complete profiles or individual rules between setups and cities; copies can be edited independently. Switching profiles keeps existing roads unchanged until you apply city rules or use the road tool. Save your city to retain its profile library.
Surface appearance depends on the road geometry and the selected surface assets. When reporting a problem, include a screenshot, the road type and the surface pack used.

ChangeLog.Value:
# Version 0.5.39
Combines all changes from versions 0.5.36 through 0.5.39 into one update.
## Default and city styling profiles
- Saves General rules, Segment rules and named styling profiles with each city. Adds a Styling profile selector and a Profiles tab to create, rename, duplicate and delete profiles. Each city remembers its selected profile. - Makes the user's shared library from before the update the starting **Default**, including all General rules, Segment rules and saved segment update preferences. Captures this setup once in settings, including when it is empty. - Starts cities without profiles with an independent Default. Create an empty profile or duplicate Default for a different city's style. Changes in one city do not alter another city's profiles or the original Default setup. - Loading a city that already has profiles uses its saved library without adding an imported profile. Renaming or deleting a city's Default does not recreate it. The original Default remains available for deliberate copying. - Copies complete profiles or individual General/Segment rules between profiles and cities. Rule cards offer **Copy to profile**. Copies receive independent rule identities; copying a rule appends it without replacing the destination's existing rules. - Keeps matching saved segment links, update preferences and differing saved road definitions. Presets in inactive profiles remain available to their linked roads, and missing surface names remain identified. - Switching profiles keeps applied road finishes. General rules still require **Apply city rules**; Segment rules still use the road tool and each preset's update preference.
## Profile deletion fix
- Fixes deleting the active profile disabling every tab and leaving the dropdown with a missing profile ID. - Selects a remaining profile before removing the old entry and automatically recovers an invalid saved selection. At least one profile must remain. - Keeps applied road finishes, junction choices and independent editable areas when removing a profile.
## UI overhaul and more intuitive tools
- Simplifies **General rules**, **Segment rules** and the tools panel, removing redundant switches, lane-handling menus and old selected-road junction controls. - Adds thumbnail previews beside surface choices and selected finishes. Previews load as choices come into view; unavailable thumbnails show **No image**. - Filters surface pickers to installed assets that support rendering over roads. Existing saved choices are retained, with a warning when a finish cannot render over roads. - Includes **Original finish** for every surface target. Sidewalks, bike lanes and bus lanes also offer **Use road pavement** alongside custom surfaces in both rule editors. - **Use road pavement** follows the pavement chosen for that specific segment, including its segment-rule override. Changing the road finish also updates linked targets. Links survive saving, preset updates and road splits or replacements. - Checking a target reveals its surface picker. Unchecking a target in a segment preset removes its local override so existing settings can apply. Older presets retain their saved behavior, and explicit Original finish choices are respected when rules overlap. - Moves **Fill paved shoulders with bus-lane surface** beneath the Bus lanes picker, visible only when Bus lanes is checked. It requires a custom bus finish; Original finish and Use road pavement turn separate shoulder filling off.
## Click junctions directly
- **Cycle junction surface** now activates a tool for clicking junctions and roundabouts directly. Hover to highlight the target and see its current finish; each left-click cycles once. - The tool stays active across repeated clicks and different junctions. Right-click or choose **Exit junction tool** to leave. - **Restore automatic** uses the same direct targeting, with modes switchable from the active tool panel. Selecting an approach road or choosing its nearest/other end is no longer required. - Retains saved junction choices, bus-lane cycling options and protected bike surfaces.
## Easier editing of generated surfaces
- Choose **Make generated surfaces editable**, then click a completed road segment. Its surfaces become independent areas and the editor opens automatically, without a material picker or an Apply changes step. - Reshaping preserves each area's existing finish, including different pavement, sidewalk, bike and bus surfaces on the same segment. - Adds **Edit another segment** and **Finish editing** controls. Right-click cancels a drag; right-click while idle leaves the editor. - Keeps the editing session focused on converted areas and supports previously converted surfaces. Other roads continue generating automatically. - Manual edits remain independent through rebuilds, rule changes, road changes, road removal and vanilla restoration. **Resume automatic surfaces** reactivates saved road rules while keeping independent areas. - Roads still generating are left untouched with a message so conversion can be retried when ready.
## Junction, roundabout and highway fixes
- Improves automatic junction and roundabout filling using eligible finishes from connected roads, including highway-only junctions and mixed street/highway approaches. - Updates connected junction approaches when road finishes change, including cases where the reference road itself has no custom finish. - Repairs recoverable saved junction references that incorrectly reported **Saved surface is unavailable**, and rebuilds affected approaches automatically when a city loads. Saves stable asset names to improve recovery on later loads. - Retains choices from genuinely missing surface packs and retries recovery when those assets return. The junction tool shows the saved asset name when known. - Fixes triangular coverage gaps at acute highway merges, splits and angled junctions. Marked crosswalk cutoffs, lane protection, planted areas, saved junction finishes and independent manual areas retain their existing behavior.
## After updating
- Restart with the updated build and reload the city. Save the city to retain its profiles, chosen setup and recovered junction identities. - Use **Rebuild applied surfaces** once to apply the junction and highway coverage improvements to existing automatic surfaces. Independent manual areas are kept. - Save General-rule edits, then choose **Apply city rules** when ready. Segment presets retain their preference for updating roads already using that preset. - If a saved surface pack is actually missing, reinstall it or choose a replacement with the junction tool. - To edit an entire junction or roundabout, convert its approach segments using **Edit another segment**. Converted areas still need Road Surface Filler and their surface assets enabled. Automatic painting resumes only through **Resume automatic surfaces**. - Version 0.5.39 is a GitHub source update; it has not been published to PDX Mods. The local build and 20 focused profile/data checks passed. Native city save/load and vertex editing still need in-game confirmation.
